purpose: Generalize the committed split mass gate to a differentiably regularly varying high-X class, derive the exact asymptotic tradeoff among mediator range, healthy chi amplitude, and bounded-source capacity, recover the committed p=2 result, and adjudicate whether the result is a credible second publication lead without claiming historical novelty, full action health, or observational success.

theory_class.gate_class: Z(X)>0 is C2 and differentiably regularly varying: Z/(z*X^s)->1, X*Z_X/Z->s, and X^2*Z_XX/Z->s*(s-1), with z>0 and s>1/2
theory_class.frozen_response_scope: Static constant-X R3 Yukawa response with frozen delta_phi, or the formal homogeneous/long-wavelength limit; spatially varying coefficients and active phi-chi mixing are outside this theorem.
theory_class.source_identity: For the committed universal conformal metric, Q_chi=-(partial_chi ln A)*T_E; the theorem leaves the physical relation between T_E and X unspecified.

asymptotic_theorem.universal_product: Q_max*ell~sqrt(Y0)*min[sqrt(2*A_infinity/s),sqrt(2*B_infinity/(s*(2*s-1)))]*sqrt(X); its exponent and leading cancellation of m_chi and z are independent of the gate amplitude and power.
asymptotic_theorem.critical_source_exponent: For a homogeneous/long-wave source |Q_chi|~q*X^r, r_c=(s+1)/2: r<r_c is asymptotically subcritical, r=r_c is coefficient-dependent, and r>r_c is asymptotically supercritical.
asymptotic_theorem.no_free_range_corollary: To keep a source X^r strictly subcritical by choosing the gate power requires s>2*r-1; the bare range must then shrink faster than X^[-(r-1/2)]. Increasing asymptotic source capacity necessarily increases range suppression.
asymptotic_theorem.sharpness_boundary: The exponent classification is exact for the homogeneous/formal k=0 response and is a sufficient bounded-source guarantee on the frozen R3 problem. Exceeding the sup-norm ceiling is not a necessary failure condition for arbitrary sign-changing or localized sources.
asymptotic_theorem.full_coupled_boundary: The bare range is not the general coupled pole when first-derivative phi-chi mixing is active. No full-action causality, hyperbolicity, cutoff, or nonlinear preservation theorem follows.

shifted_power_family.definition: Z=(1+beta*X^2)^p with beta>0 and p>1/4, so s=2*p
shifted_power_family.committed_recovery: p=2 gives ell~X^-2, chi_max~X^-3/2, Q_max~X^5/2, exactly recovering the committed split-gate source-bound package.
shifted_power_family.interpretation: p>1/2 is required if the healthy chi-amplitude ceiling itself is to shrink at high X; p>1/4 is enough for the K-branch asymptotic coefficient to remain positive.

fifth_force_link.restricted_ratio: epsilon_chi(r)=2*alpha_chi^2*(1+r/ell)*exp(-r/ell)/Y0 for the committed constant-coefficient point-source subcase
fifth_force_link.fixed_distance_limit: For every fixed r>0 and s>0, ell->0 and epsilon_chi(r)->0 as X->infinity.
fifth_force_link.tradeoff: The same s that increases the source ceiling exponent also exponentially suppresses the restricted fifth force at fixed distance.
fifth_force_link.not_claimed: This does not screen phi, solve a material body, prove thin-shell behavior, or establish a Solar-System pass.

primary_literature_positioning.relevance: Environment-dependent mediator mass and range are established screening concepts, but the mass is controlled by matter density rather than a second field's kinetic invariant.
Density-dependent symmetry restoration screens the coupling; it is a distinct mechanism from the derivative-controlled mass gate and does not provide this range-source exponent identity.
Nonlinear kinetic self-interactions screen a scalar force; the present class instead keeps chi kinetic normalization constant and gates its mass through X.
Kinetically dependent conformal couplings and ultralocal screening are nearby prior art, but not an identified exact rewrite of the split mass-gate range-source theorem.
Modern kinetic-screening two-body analyses expose geometry-dependent screened and descreened regions, reinforcing that the frozen constant-coefficient theorem is not a full nonlinear source solution.
